Clause delivery-earns-its-own-signals and the evaluator's signal rule (d0010-dual-signal-exact-target, minimum_independent_reports: 2) require two independent, mechanically applicable, admitted reports over the exact integrated product tree with the trl2 guards executing inside both. The conformance-suite extension is the emission proof the guards verify — the predicate's 'machine core' — not obviously a second signal channel sitting alongside the check-set pass; if the conformance run is what makes guard-emits-at-death accept, then the two 'signals' as glossed are not independent channels and the guards do not execute inside both. As written, the gloss could lead the design stage to mis-pin the dual-signal structure (treating the suite extension as one of the two reports rather than the substance both independent reports verify). This is an imprecision, not a contradiction: the proposal still binds two independent admitted signals, the full trl2-guards set, and all_nodes_accept, so no clause is falsified.","proposed_disposition":"At the design stage (or in a proposal touch-up), restate the signal pair as two independent mechanical reports over the exact integrated product tree, each executing the registered trl2-guards check set, with the conformance-suite extension positioned as the emission evidence both reports verify — matching the evaluator's signal_rule and the clause's 'guards executing inside both' wording."},{"id":"finding

When the staged base is anchored (00-base-pin present — the pre-lineage git-anchored base the driver's new staging branch creates via gitanchor.HeadProduct, and every anchor-preserving product head, since ApplyBatch preserves base.Anchor), the executor parses the PIN body as the base: base = ParseProduct(basePinBody), so ApplyBatch yields linked = {Anchor, Files: overlay-union} and out.ResultTreeHash = TreeHash of that anchored body. Every downstream consumer computes the EXPANDED tree hash instead: deriveResultTreeHash (in this same change-set) expands an anchored base before Apply ('the derived hash equals the verifier's materialized tree hash'), the code-tree verifier materializes the expanded base + diff, and the receipt binds MaterializedTreeHash. For any non-empty anchored tree the anchored-body hash can never equal the expanded hash, so the assembly output fails evaluateChangeSetResultTree ('change set result tree differs from derived tree') at the default packet-checks gate and can never earn a verification signal. The deterministic assembly pass — the delivery of work-graph-integrated@2 clause subject-assembly-is-deterministic, whose own text says 'composing those heads over the anchored base' — therefore produces stillborn change-sets in the anchored-base regime.
